artifact: Surface v12 SaaS V1 structured builder attempt 7
conclusion: Pass: this is a valid, coherent structured wireframe for the SaaS V1 minimum-live surface. It is not runtime qualification.

checks.evidence: The onboarding route has a definition-backed setup form with organization, workspace, and production/sandbox environment fields; its content names teammate invitations and assisted SSO/SAML/SCIM. The route transitions to Dashboard.

Forms, parameterized form detail, preview, and public respondent routes represent templates/Studio import, publish/share/version pinning, preview, anonymous completion, validation/review/confirmation, and a definition-backed mobile response form.
Responses route names tenant responses and CSV/JSON export and binds the structured query:responses public resource, whose schema includes responses, export formats, and proof status.

Signature workflows represent envelopes, status, reminders, completion, and certificates. Public receipt represents a receipt and verifier-backed proof status, while hosted general verification is explicitly disabled.
Organization administration explicitly covers organization, workspaces, roles, invitations, branding, and feature visibility, with assisted and disabled governance states named.
The integrations route explicitly covers API keys, generated API docs, sandbox/test, one webhook, and delivery history, with connectors preview and large imports assisted.
Billing names plan limits, usage, billing status, and entitlements and binds host:billing, a structured host-state resource with plan, usage, limits, and billing-status schema.

Support/trust names status, support, incident records, trust center, and subprocessors and binds resource:support-trust, whose schema covers service status, incidents, support access, and trust documents.

Every represented area uses explicit LIVE, ASSISTED, PREVIEW, or DISABLED language, including collaborative authoring, SSO, bulk export, identity proofing, witness/notary, connectors, retention/legal hold, DSAR, dedicated review, active-active, and hosted verification.

The surface has 13 routes and 21 transitions. Dashboard links to seven primary destinations; the form detail route is parameterized by formId and its transitions supply frm_annual-intake. The public completion path connects to receipt and then proof/support.

The exported bundle contains a definition with seven required fields, an experience unit with four completion steps, 11 response actions, a reusable registered widget mounted on all 13 routes, and three typed data-source resources bound to responses, billing, and support/trust.

remaining_limitations: This score does not establish persistence, tenant isolation, authentication/session recovery, billing execution, entitlement enforcement, webhook delivery, signature or receipt generation, email delivery, or browser behavior.
The validation report did not run surface-local, authorization-boundary, or unsupported-feature phases.
Most SaaS journey detail is represented as structured route content and action graph rather than executable controls or backend behavior.
The single shared definition is reused for organization setup and public response, so it demonstrates form structure but not production-specific form schemas or field-level journey separation.
